title: Ceiling bound for the solver exponent
statement: Let $\omega$ be a positive rational number and let $k$ be a natural number. If $c=\lceil \omega k/(\omega+1)\rceil$, then $\lceil \omega\,(k-c)\rceil\le c$, where the subtraction $k-c$ is truncated subtraction on the natural numbers.
